resources.string: Press firmly and directly on the wound to stop the bleeding.
Call emergency services immediately for heavy bleeding. Do not wait.

string-array.name: case_bleeding_steps
string-array.item: Wear gloves if available, and have the person sit or lie down.
Press firmly on the wound with a clean cloth or gauze.
Keep pressing without lifting your hand to check. If the cloth soaks through, add another on top.
Raise the injured limb if possible and secure a firm bandage over the cloth.
Stay with the person until help arrives and watch their breathing and alertness.

string-array.name: case_bleeding_donts
string-array.item: Do not remove a soaked cloth. Add a new one on top.
Do not pull out an object stuck in the wound.
Do not use a tourniquet unless direct pressure fails to stop life-threatening bleeding from a limb.

resources.string: Cool the burn under cool running water for 10 to 20 minutes.
Call emergency services if the burn is large or deep, on the face, hands, genitals or over a joint, affects a child or an older person, or was caused by chemicals or electricity.

string-array.name: case_burns_steps
string-array.item: Move the person away from the heat source and put out any flames.
Cool the burn with cool or lukewarm running water (not icy) for 10 to 20 minutes.
Remove rings, watches and tight items near the burn before swelling starts, unless stuck to the skin.
Cover the burn loosely with clean gauze or plastic cling film.
Get medical advice if you are unsure how serious the burn is.

string-array.name: case_burns_donts
string-array.item: Do not apply ice or icy water.
Do not pop blisters.
Do not apply toothpaste, butter, oil or creams.
Do not remove clothing stuck to the skin.

resources.string: Wash the wound with clean running water and cover it with a clean dressing.
See a doctor if the cut is deep, very dirty, keeps bleeding, or if the person has not had a tetanus vaccine for many years.

string-array.name: case_cut_steps
string-array.item: Wash your hands with soap and water before touching the wound.
Press on the cut with a clean cloth until the bleeding stops.
Rinse the wound under clean running water to remove dirt.
Gently dry around it and cover with a clean dressing or gauze.
Change the dressing daily and watch for redness, swelling or pus.

string-array.name: case_cut_donts
string-array.item: Do not pour alcohol or hydrogen peroxide into the wound.
Do not touch the wound with unwashed hands.
